subject: literature
passage: For a year, Teodora had copied the master's charts in his Lisbon workshop, tracing each bay and cape with a fine pen until her lines matched his exactly. This morning, though, a sailor who came in insisted that a sandbar now blocked the mouth of the river shown on the chart she was finishing. The master was away. Teodora hesitated, her pen above the paper, then asked the sailor to describe the sandbar's shape and position. Slowly, for the first time, she drew a line that appeared on no chart the master had ever made.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Teodora refuses to change the chart until her master returns to the workshop.
choices.B: Teodora learns from a sailor how sandbars form at the mouths of rivers.
choices.C: Teodora realizes that all of her master's charts are full of careless errors.
choices.D: Teodora moves from copying her master's work to relying on her own judgment.

explanation.why: At first Teodora copies the master's charts "until her lines matched his exactly." When the master is away and the sailor reports a new sandbar, she decides on her own to add it, drawing "a line that appeared on no chart the master had ever made." The text shows her shift from copying to independent judgment.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Teodora hesitates but then draws the sandbar while the master is still away.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sailor describes the sandbar's shape and position, not how sandbars form.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sailor reports one new sandbar; the text never says the master's charts are full of careless errors.
explanation.D: Correct. This covers the whole text: a year of exact copying followed by her first independent change.
